newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian term lenders cut prime rate to 16.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indian term lenders cut prime rate to 16.5 pct.

text.p: Indian term lending institutions have cut their prime lending rate to 16.5 percent per annum from 17.0 percent with immediate effect, the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) said on Wednesday.

"All-India financial institutions have decided to reduce the minimum lending rate from 17.0 percent per annum (exclusive of interest tax) to 16.5 percent with effect from October 23, 1996," IDBI said in a statement.

IDBI is India's largest term lending institution. The IDBI statement also included other long-term lenders -- Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India, SCICI Ltd and Industrial Finance Corp of India.
"Simultaneously, the interest rate band has been reduced to 3.5 percentage points from 4.0 percentage points," it said.
As a result, the interest rate at the top of the band will stand reduced by one percentage point, IDBI said.
